title: In a taxi
subtitle: Transportation · destination · payment

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
승객: 기사님, 부산역으로 가 주세요.
기사: 부산역 몇 번 출구로 가실까요?
승객: 일단 부산역 주변으로 가 주세요.
기사: 알겠습니다.

…

승객: 여기서 내릴게요. 카드도 되나요?
기사: 네, 됩니다.
승객: 여기 있습니다.
기사: 감사합니다. 안녕히 가세요.
승객: 감사합니다.
blocks.speakable: 기사님, 부산역으로 가 주세요.  부산역 몇 번 출구로 가실까요?  일단 부산역 주변으로 가 주세요.   알겠습니다.   여기서 내릴게요. 카드도 되나요?   네, 됩니다.  여기 있습니다.   감사합니다. 안녕히 가세요.  감사합니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Passenger: Please take me to Busan Station.
Driver: Which exit at Busan Station would you like to go to?
Passenger: Please take me near Busan Station for now.
Driver: All right.

…

Passenger: I’ll get out here. Can I pay by card?
Driver: Yes, you can.
Passenger: Here you are.
Driver: Thank you. Goodbye.
Passenger: Thank you.

blocks.label: Key expressions
blocks.text:
~(으)로 가 주세요.
ro ga juseyo

여기서 내릴게요.
yeogi

~ 되나요?
~ doenayo

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A passenger asks to go to Busan Station. The driver asks for a specific exit, but the passenger does not know the exact location and asks to go near the station first. At the end of the ride, the passenger asks to stop, checks whether card payment is available, pays, and exchanges polite goodbyes with the driver.

title: At a restaurant
subtitle: Restaurant · ordering food

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
직원: 몇 분이세요?
나: 두 명이요.
직원: 이쪽으로 앉으세요.
직원: 주문하시겠어요?
나: 좀 이따가 부를게요. 감사합니다.
직원: 네, 알겠습니다.

친구: 3인분 먹을까? 아니면 2인분?
나: 2인분만 하자.
친구: 그래.

나: 저기요, 주문할게요.
직원: 네, 말씀하세요.
나: 삼겹살 2인분하고 밥 두 공기 주세요.
직원: 음료는 뭐로 드릴까요?
나: 사이다 한 병 주세요.
직원: 네, 알겠습니다.
blocks.speakable: 몇 분이세요?  두 명이요.   이쪽으로 앉으세요.   주문하시겠어요?  좀 이따가 부를게요. 감사합니다.  네, 알겠습니다.  3인분 먹을까? 아니면 2인분?   2인분만 하자.   그래.    저기요, 주문할게요.   네, 말씀하세요.   삼겹살 2인분하고 밥 두 공기 주세요.   음료는 뭐로 드릴까요?    사이다 한 병 주세요.   네, 알겠습니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Staff: How many people?
Me: Two.
Staff: Please have a seat over here.
Staff: Are you ready to order?
Me: We'll call you in a little while. Thank you.
Staff: Certainly.

Friend: Three servings? Or two?
Me: Let's just get two servings.
Friend: Okay.

Me: Excuse me, we'd like to order.
Staff: Certainly, go ahead.
Me: Two servings of pork belly and two bowls of rice, please.
Staff: What would you like to drink?
Me: One bottle of Sprite, please.
Staff: Certainly.

blocks.label: Key expressions
blocks.text:
몇 분이세요?
myeot bun-iseyo

좀 이따가 부를게요.
jom ittdaga bureulgeyo

주문할게요.
jumunhalgeyo

삼겹살 2인분, 밥 두 공기
samgyeopsal i-inbun, bap du gonggi

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: Two friends enter a restaurant and are shown to a table. They decide to choose their food before ordering, then call the staff when they are ready. They order two servings of pork belly, two bowls of rice, and a bottle of soda.

title: At a Cafe
subtitle: Ordering · size · takeaway · payment

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
손님: 안녕하세요.
직원: 어서 오세요.
손님: 아이스 아메리카노 한 잔 주세요.
직원: 라지로 드릴까요?
손님: 네, 라지로 주세요.
직원: 드시고 가시나요, 가지고 가시나요?
손님: 가지고 갈게요.
직원: 5,500원입니다.
손님: 카드로 계산할게요.
직원: 감사합니다. 주문번호는 37번입니다.
손님: 감사합니다.
blocks.speakable: 안녕하세요. 어서 오세요. 아이스 아메리카노 한 잔 주세요. 라지로 드릴까요? 네, 라지로 주세요. 드시고 가시나요, 가지고 가시나요? 가지고 갈게요. 5,500원입니다. 카드로 계산할게요. 감사합니다. 주문번호는 37번입니다. 감사합니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Customer: Hello.
Staff: Welcome.
Customer: I'd like one iced Americano, please.
Staff: Would you like a large size?
Customer: Yes, a large, please.
Staff: For here or to go?
Customer: To go, please.
Staff: That'll be 5,500 won.
Customer: I'll pay by card.
Staff: Thank you. Your order number is 37.
Customer: Thank you.

blocks.label: Key Expressions
blocks.text:
N 한 잔 주세요.
...han jan juseyo

가지고 갈게요.
gajigo galgeyo

카드로 계산할게요.
kadeuro gyesanhalgeyo

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A customer orders an iced Americano at a cafe. The staff asks about the drink size and whether the order is for here or to go. After confirming the order, the customer pays by card, receives an order number, and politely ends the conversation.

title: At a Clothing Store
subtitle: Shopping · fitting · payment

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
손님: 안녕하세요.
직원: 어서 오세요. 찾으시는 게 있으세요?
손님: 셔츠를 보고 싶은데요.
직원: 이쪽에 있습니다.
손님: 이거 입어 봐도 될까요?
직원: 네. 탈의실은 저쪽입니다.

…

손님: 잘 맞네요. 이걸로 살게요.
직원: 계산 도와드리겠습니다.
손님: 카드로 계산할게요.
직원: 감사합니다.
손님: 감사합니다.
blocks.speakable: 안녕하세요. 어서 오세요. 찾으시는 게 있으세요? 셔츠를 보고 싶은데요. 이쪽에 있습니다. 이거 입어 봐도 될까요? 네. 탈의실은 저쪽입니다. 잘 맞네요. 이걸로 살게요. 계산 도와드리겠습니다. 카드로 계산할게요. 감사합니다. 감사합니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Customer: Hello.
Staff: Welcome. May I help you?
Customer: I'd like to look at some shirts.
Staff: They're over here.
Customer: May I try this on?
Staff: Of course. The fitting room is over there.

...

Customer: It fits well. I'll take this one.
Staff: I'll ring it up for you.
Customer: I'll pay by card.
Staff: Thank you.
Customer: Thank you.

blocks.label: Key Expressions
blocks.text:
N를 보고 싶은데요.
...reul bogo sipeundeyo

입어 봐도 될까요?
ibeo bwado doelkkayo

이걸로 살게요.
igeollo salgeyo

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A customer visits a clothing store to buy a shirt. After asking where the shirts are, the customer tries one on in the fitting room. Since it fits well, the customer decides to buy it, pays by card, and politely finishes the conversation.

title: At a Hospital (Cold)
subtitle: Reception · symptoms · prescription

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
접수: 어떻게 오셨나요?
환자: 감기 증상이 있어서 왔어요.
접수: 잠시만 기다려 주세요.

…

의사: 어디가 불편하세요?
환자: 기침이 나고 목이 아파요.
의사: 열은 있으세요?
환자: 조금 있는 것 같아요.
의사: 감기인 것 같습니다. 약을 처방해 드릴게요.
환자: 감사합니다.
blocks.speakable: 어떻게 오셨나요? 감기 증상이 있어서 왔어요. 잠시만 기다려 주세요. 어디가 불편하세요? 기침이 나고 목이 아파요. 열은 있으세요? 조금 있는 것 같아요. 감기인 것 같습니다. 약을 처방해 드릴게요. 감사합니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Receptionist: What brings you in today?
Patient: I came because I have cold symptoms.
Receptionist: Please wait a moment.

...

Doctor: What seems to be the problem?
Patient: I have a cough and a sore throat.
Doctor: Do you have a fever?
Patient: I think I have a slight fever.
Doctor: It looks like you have a cold. I'll prescribe some medicine.
Patient: Thank you.

blocks.label: Key Expressions
blocks.text:
감기 증상이 있어서 왔어요.
gamgi jeungsangi isseoseo wasseoyo

어디가 불편하세요?
eodiga bulpyeonhaseyo

약을 처방해 드릴게요.
yageul cheobanghae deurilgeyo

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A patient visits a clinic because of cold symptoms. After checking in at the reception desk, the patient waits to see the doctor, explains the symptoms, and is diagnosed with a cold. The doctor prescribes medicine, and the conversation ends politely.

title: At a Hospital (Sprained Ankle)
subtitle: Reception · injury · treatment

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
접수: 어떻게 오셨나요?
환자: 계단에서 발목을 삐었어요.
접수: 잠시만 기다려 주세요.

…

의사: 많이 아프세요?
환자: 걸을 때 많이 아파요.
의사: 발목을 한번 보겠습니다.
환자: 네.
의사: 심한 염좌는 아닌 것 같습니다. 당분간 무리하지 마세요.
환자: 감사합니다.
blocks.speakable: 어떻게 오셨나요? 계단에서 발목을 삐었어요. 잠시만 기다려 주세요. 많이 아프세요? 걸을 때 많이 아파요. 발목을 한번 보겠습니다. 네. 심한 염좌는 아닌 것 같습니다. 당분간 무리하지 마세요. 감사합니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Receptionist: What brings you in today?
Patient: I sprained my ankle on the stairs.
Receptionist: Please wait a moment.

...

Doctor: Does it hurt a lot?
Patient: It hurts when I walk.
Doctor: Let me take a look at your ankle.
Patient: Okay.
Doctor: It doesn't seem to be a severe sprain. Please avoid strenuous activity for a while.
Patient: Thank you.

blocks.label: Key Expressions
blocks.text:
발목을 삐었어요.
balmogeul ppieosseoyo

걸을 때 아파요.
georeul ttae apayo

당분간 무리하지 마세요.
dangbungan murihaji maseyo

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A patient visits a clinic after spraining an ankle on the stairs. The doctor asks about the pain, examines the ankle, and explains that it is not a serious sprain. The patient is advised to avoid strenuous activity for a while before leaving.

title: At a Hospital (Stomachache)
subtitle: Reception · stomachache · diagnosis

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
접수: 어떻게 오셨나요?
환자: 배가 많이 아파서 왔어요.
접수: 잠시만 기다려 주세요.

…

의사: 언제부터 아프셨나요?
환자: 오늘 아침부터 아팠어요.
의사: 다른 증상도 있으세요?
환자: 속이 메스껍고 밥도 잘 못 먹겠어요.
의사: 위장염인 것 같습니다. 약을 처방해 드릴게요.
환자: 감사합니다.
blocks.speakable: 어떻게 오셨나요? 배가 많이 아파서 왔어요. 잠시만 기다려 주세요. 언제부터 아프셨나요? 오늘 아침부터 아팠어요. 다른 증상도 있으세요? 속이 메스껍고 밥도 잘 못 먹겠어요. 위장염인 것 같습니다. 약을 처방해 드릴게요. 감사합니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Receptionist: What brings you in today?
Patient: I came because I have a bad stomachache.
Receptionist: Please wait a moment.

...

Doctor: When did the pain start?
Patient: It started this morning.
Doctor: Do you have any other symptoms?
Patient: I feel nauseous, and I can't eat very well.
Doctor: It looks like you have gastroenteritis. I'll prescribe some medicine.
Patient: Thank you.

blocks.label: Key Expressions
blocks.text:
배가 많이 아파서 왔어요.
baega mani apaseo wasseoyo

언제부터 아프셨나요?
eonjebuteo apeusyeonnayo

속이 메스꺼워요.
sogi meseukkeowoyo

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A patient visits a clinic because of a stomachache. The doctor asks when the pain started and whether there are any other symptoms. After hearing that the patient feels nauseous and has trouble eating, the doctor diagnoses gastroenteritis and prescribes medicine.

title: At a Pharmacy
subtitle: Prescription · medicine · directions

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
손님: 안녕하세요.
약사: 안녕하세요.
손님: 처방전을 가지고 왔어요.
약사: 처방전 주세요.
손님: 여기 있습니다.
약사: 하루 세 번, 식후에 드시면 됩니다.
손님: 주의할 점이 있나요?
약사: 물을 충분히 드시고, 졸릴 수 있으니 운전은 피하세요.
손님: 알겠습니다. 감사합니다.
약사: 빨리 나으세요.
blocks.speakable: 안녕하세요. 안녕하세요. 처방전을 가지고 왔어요. 처방전 주세요. 여기 있습니다. 하루 세 번, 식후에 드시면 됩니다. 주의할 점이 있나요? 물을 충분히 드시고, 졸릴 수 있으니 운전은 피하세요. 알겠습니다. 감사합니다. 빨리 나으세요.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Customer: Hello.
Pharmacist: Hello.
Customer: I have a prescription.
Pharmacist: May I have your prescription, please?
Customer: Here you are.
Pharmacist: Take this medicine three times a day after meals.
Customer: Is there anything I should be careful about?
Pharmacist: Drink plenty of water, and avoid driving because it may make you drowsy.
Customer: I understand. Thank you.
Pharmacist: Get well soon.

blocks.label: Key Expressions
blocks.text:
처방전을 가지고 왔어요.
cheobangjeoneul gajigo wasseoyo

하루 세 번, 식후에 드시면 됩니다.
haru se beon, sikhue deusimyeon doemnida

주의할 점이 있나요?
juihal jeomi innayo

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A customer visits a pharmacy with a prescription from a clinic. The pharmacist explains how to take the medicine and gives some precautions. After asking one question, the customer thanks the pharmacist and leaves.

title: Delivery Problem
subtitle: Customer service · package · delivery

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
고객: 안녕하세요. 택배가 아직 도착하지 않았어요.
상담원: 불편을 드려 죄송합니다. 송장번호를 알려주시겠어요?
고객: 123456789입니다.
상담원: 잠시만 확인해 보겠습니다.

…

상담원: 배송이 지연되고 있습니다. 오늘 안에 배송될 예정입니다.
고객: 알겠습니다. 감사합니다.
상담원: 기다려 주셔서 감사합니다.
blocks.speakable: 안녕하세요. 택배가 아직 도착하지 않았어요. 불편을 드려 죄송합니다. 송장번호를 알려주시겠어요? 123456789입니다. 잠시만 확인해 보겠습니다. 배송이 지연되고 있습니다. 오늘 안에 배송될 예정입니다. 알겠습니다. 감사합니다. 기다려 주셔서 감사합니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Customer: Hello. My package hasn't arrived yet.
Agent: We're sorry for the inconvenience. Could you tell me the tracking number?
Customer: It's 123456789.
Agent: Let me check that for you.

...

Agent: Your delivery has been delayed. It is expected to arrive today.
Customer: I understand. Thank you.
Agent: Thank you for your patience.

blocks.label: Key Expressions
blocks.text:

baesongi jiyeondoego itseumnida

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A customer contacts customer service because a package has not arrived. After checking the tracking number, the agent explains that the delivery has been delayed and is expected to arrive later that day. The conversation ends politely.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A customer visits a convenience store to buy a phone charger. After asking whether the store has one, the staff asks which type is needed. The customer chooses a USB-C charger, pays by card, and politely ends the conversation.

title: At a Tourist Attraction
subtitle: Asking for directions · restroom

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
관광객: 실례합니다.
안내원: 네. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
관광객: 화장실이 어디에 있나요?
안내원: 저쪽으로 쭉 가시면 오른쪽에 있습니다.
관광객: 멀어요?
안내원: 아니요. 1분 정도 걸립니다.
관광객: 감사합니다.
안내원: 천만에요. 좋은 관람 되세요.
관광객: 감사합니다.
blocks.speakable: 실례합니다. 네. 무엇을 도와드릴까요? 화장실이 어디에 있나요? 저쪽으로 쭉 가시면 오른쪽에 있습니다. 멀어요? 아니요. 1분 정도 걸립니다. 감사합니다. 천만에요. 좋은 관람 되세요. 감사합니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Visitor: Excuse me.
Staff: Yes. How can I help you?
Visitor: Where is the restroom?
Staff: Go straight that way, and you'll find it on your right.
Visitor: Is it far?
Staff: No. It's about a one-minute walk.
Visitor: Thank you.
Staff: You're welcome. Enjoy your visit.
Visitor: Thank you.

blocks.label: Key Expressions
blocks.text:
화장실이 어디에 있나요?
hwajangsiri eodie innayo

쭉 가시면 됩니다.
jjuk gasimyeon doemnida

멀어요?
meoreoyo

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A visitor asks for the location of the restroom at a tourist attraction. The staff gives simple directions and explains that it is only a short walk away. After receiving the information, the visitor thanks the staff, who wishes the visitor an enjoyable visit.

title: 좋다 / 나쁘다
subtitle: Basic evaluative contrast

blocks.label: Positive
blocks.text:
좋아요.

좋은 생각 nice idea

좋은 느낌 good feeling

좋은 사람 nice person

좋은 시점 exact timing

좋은 마음 warm heart
blocks.speakable: 좋아요. 좋은 생각. 좋은 느낌. 좋은 사람. 좋은 시점. 좋은 마음.

blocks.label: Negative
blocks.text:
나빠요.

나쁜 기분 bad feeling

나쁜 사람 bad person

나쁜 의도 ill intention

나쁜 상태 bad condition

나쁜 선택 wrong choice

나쁜 말 harful words
blocks.speakable: 나빠요. 나쁜 기분. 나쁜 사람. 나쁜 의도. 나쁜 상태. 나쁜 선택. 나쁜 말.

blocks.label: Context
blocks.text: These words evaluate things, conditions, decisions, health, weather, and many other topics.

title: 예쁘다 / 아름답다
subtitle: Similar meaning, different scope and tone

blocks.label: 예쁘다
blocks.text: 예뻐요. It looks pretty.
blocks.speakable: 예뻐요. 아름다워요.

blocks.label: 아름답다
blocks.text: 아름다워요. That's beauty

blocks.label: Difference
blocks.text: 예쁘다 is common and everyday. 아름답다 is broader and often more elevated or literary.

title: 비가 오다 → 우산을 가져가다
subtitle: A natural situation-to-action connection

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: 비가 와요. It's raining.
blocks.speakable: 비가 와요. 우산을 가져가요.

blocks.label: Likely action
blocks.text: (그러니) 우산을 가져가요. So you'll take the umbrella

blocks.label: Why it matters
blocks.text: This section connects words through ordinary expectations rather than dictionary definitions alone.

title: 손이 크다
subtitle: To prepare or give more than expected

blocks.label: Expression
blocks.text: 우리 어머니는 손이 커요.
blocks.speakable: 우리 어머니는 손이 커요.

blocks.label: Meaning
blocks.text: She tends to prepare a lot, especially food. It does not literally describe hand size.

blocks.label: Scene
blocks.text: A meal for three people becomes enough food for ten.

title: Notice
subtitle: The speaker notices or recognizes something in the moment.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “Oh, I notice that...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
덥네. → It's hot.

싫네. → I don't like it.

잘 아네. → So you konw it.

좋네. → It's good.

빠르네. → It's fast.
blocks.speakable: 덥네.  싫네.  잘 아네.  좋네.   빠르네.

blocks.label: Naturalness
blocks.text: Some combinations are grammatically possible but uncommon without a suitable context. For example, '믿네' may sound marked or incomplete in ordinary conversation.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker encounters new information, notices a quality, or reacts to something happening in front of them.

title: Shared Knowledge
subtitle: The speaker treats the information as something both people know or can agree on.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “You know that too, right?”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
덥죠? → It's hot. right?

싫죠? → You don't like it. right?

믿죠? → You belive it right?

알죠? → You know it. Right?

맞죠. → It's correct. Right?
blocks.speakable: 덥죠?  싫죠?   믿죠?   알죠?   맞죠?

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker presents the statement as mutually accessible information and often expects agreement or confirmation from the listener.

title: Realization
subtitle: The speaker reaches a new understanding.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “Ah, now I understand...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
덥구나. → So it's truely hot.

그렇구나. → So that's it.

이 사람이 담당자군요. → So he is the person in the charge.

생각보다 멀군요. → So it is further than I thought.
blocks.speakable: 덥구나.  그렇구나.  이 사람이 담당자군요.   생각보다 멀군요.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker processes new information and expresses the moment of understanding or realization.

title: Guess
subtitle: The speaker infers something from available signs or circumstances.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “I suppose...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
덥겠네요. → It looks hot.

힘들겠네요. → It looks hard.

많이 바쁜가 봐요*. → You look quite busy.

비가 오겠네요. → It seems it will rain.
blocks.speakable: 덥겠네요.  힘들겠네요.   많이 바쁜가 봐요.   비가 오겠네요.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker does not state the information as directly observed fact, but infers it from context, appearance, or prior information.

title: Insistence
subtitle: The speaker repeats or reinforces a claim.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “I'm telling you...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
덥다니까. → I'm serious it's hot!

맞다니까. → I'm no lying!

괜찮다니까. → I'm surely fine!

진짜라니까. → It's really true!
blocks.speakable: 덥다니까.  맞다니까.   괜찮다니까.   진짜라니까.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker strengthens a statement because the listener doubts it, disagrees, misunderstands, or has not responded appropriately.

title: Surprise
subtitle: The speaker reacts to something unexpected or more striking than anticipated.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “Oh, I didn't expect that...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
사람이 정말 많네요. → There are so many people.
생각보다 비싸군요. → It is more expensive than I expected.

벌써 다 끝났네요. → Oh, it is already finished.

한국어를 정말 잘하시네요. → You speak Korean very well.
blocks.speakable: 사람이 정말 많네요.  생각보다 비싸군요.   벌써 다 끝났네요.  한국어를 정말 잘하시네요.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker encounters something unexpected and immediately expresses surprise, admiration, or a mismatch with their previous expectation.

title: Confirmation
subtitle: The speaker checks whether their understanding or assumption is correct.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “My understanding is correct, right?”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
여기가 부산역 맞죠? → This is Busan Station, right?

내일까지 하면 되는 거죠? → I only need to finish it by tomorrow, right?

카드로 계산할 수 있나요? → Can I pay by card?

이 버스가 시청에 가는 거죠? → This bus goes to City Hall, right?
blocks.speakable: 여기가 부산역 맞죠?   내일까지 하면 되는 거죠?  카드로 계산할 수 있나요?  이 버스가 시청에 가는 거죠?

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker already has an assumption or partial understanding and asks the listener to confirm it before proceeding.

title: Reminder
subtitle: The speaker presents information as something the listener should already know or remember.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “You already know this...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
오늘 쉬는 날이잖아요. → You know today is a day off.

제가 아까 말씀드렸잖아요. → I told you earlier, remember?

여기는 주차하면 안 되잖아요. → You know we cannot park here.
그 사람 바쁜 거 알잖아요. → You know that person is busy.
blocks.speakable: 오늘 쉬는 날이잖아요.  제가 아까 말씀드렸잖아요.  여기는 주차하면 안되잖아요. 그 사람 바쁜 거 알잖아요.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker reminds the listener of information treated as already shared. Depending on tone, it may sound explanatory, persuasive, frustrated, or mildly reproachful.

title: Concession
subtitle: The speaker acknowledges one fact before introducing a limitation, contrast, or different conclusion.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “That is true, but...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
맛있기는 한데 너무 비싸요. → It is tasty, but it is too expensive.

좋기는 해요. 그런데 좀 멀어요. → It is good, but it is a little far away.

맞기는 한데 설명이 부족해요. → That is true, but the explanation is incomplete.

갈 수는 있는데 늦을 것 같아요. → I can go, but I think I will be late.
blocks.speakable: 맛있기는 한데 너무 비싸요.  좋기는 해요. 그런데 좀 멀어요.  맞기는 한데 설명이 부족해요.  갈수는 있는데 늦을 것 같아요.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker accepts part of another person's statement or recognizes a positive point, while signaling that another concern changes the overall judgment.

title: Reluctance
subtitle: The speaker hesitates, avoids a direct refusal, or signals that something is difficult to accept.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “I would rather not say no directly, but...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
오늘은 좀 어려울 것 같아요. → I do not think today will work.

그건 조금 곤란한데요. → That may be a little difficult.

지금 바로 결정하기는 좀 그래요<. → I am not comfortable deciding right now.

이번에는 참석하기 어려울 것 같습니다. → I do not think I can attend this time.
blocks.speakable: 오늘은 좀 어려울 것 같아요.  그건 조금 곤란한데요.  지금 바로 결정하기는 좀 그래요.   이번에는 참석하기 어려울 것 같습니다.

blocks.label: Pattern
blocks.text: Speaker is not confident and it follows with negative signs ★'는'(but, though) '조금(좀)'(little) '약간'(few) '살짝'(a bit) '별로'(not) '그다지'(not so much) )

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker softens a refusal or negative judgment instead of stating it bluntly. Words such as 좀 and expressions such as 것 같아요 leave room for the listener to infer the refusal.

title: Concern
subtitle: The speaker notices a possible problem and expresses worry or consideration for another person.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “I am worried about this...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
많이 힘드시겠어요. → That must be very difficult for you.

비가 많이 오는데 괜찮겠어요? → It is raining heavily. Will you be all right?

얼굴이 안 좋아 보여요. → You do not look well.

이렇게 늦어서 어떡해요? → What are we going to do now that it is so late?
blocks.speakable: 많이 힘드시겠어요.  비가 많이 오는데 괜찮겠어요?   얼굴이 안좋아 보여요.  이렇게 늦어서 어떡해요?

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker infers that another person may be experiencing difficulty or that a situation may develop badly, and responds with sympathy, worry, or caution.

title: Intention
subtitle: The speaker presents a decision, plan, or immediate course of action.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “This is what I have decided to do...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
제가 다시 전화할게요. → I will call you again.

여기서 내릴게요. → I will get out here.

제가 확인해 보겠습니다. → I will check it.

이번 주말에는 집에서 쉬려고 해요. → I am planning to rest at home this weekend.
blocks.speakable: 제가 다시 전화할게요.  여기서 내릴게요.  제가 확인해 보겠습니다.  이번 주말에는 집에서 쉬려고 해요.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker communicates a decision or plan. 할게요 often responds to the immediate situation, while 하겠습니다 can sound more formal or deliberate.

title: Expectation
subtitle: The speaker anticipates a likely event or outcome based on current knowledge.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “This will probably happen...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
오늘은 늦게 끝날 것 같아요. → I think we will finish late today.

아마 주말에는 사람이 많겠어요. → There will probably be many people on the weekend.

이 길이 더 빠를 것 같아요. → I think this road will be faster.

아마 내일 도착할 거예요. → It will probably arrive tomorrow.
blocks.speakable: 오늘은 늦게 끝날 것 같아요.  주말에는 사람이 많겠어요.  이 길이 더 빠를 것 같아요.  아마 내일 도착할 거예요.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker predicts a future event or outcome. Unlike direct observation, the statement is presented as an expectation rather than a confirmed fact.

title: Regret
subtitle: The speaker looks back on an action or missed opportunity with dissatisfaction.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “I should have done something differently...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
택시를 탈 걸 그랬어요. → I should have taken a taxi.

미리 예약할 걸 그랬네요. → I should have made a reservation earlier.

그 말을 하지 말걸 그랬어요. → I wish I had not said that.

괜히 늦게 출발했어요. → I should not have left so late.
blocks.speakable: 택시를 탈 걸 그랬어요.  미리 예약할 걸 그랬네요.  그 말을 하지 말걸 그랬어요.  괜히 늦게 출발했어요.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker evaluates a past choice negatively and imagines a better alternative that was not taken.

title: Reassurance
subtitle: The speaker tries to reduce another person's worry or resistance.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “You do not need to worry...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
괜찮아요. 천천히 하세요. → It is all right. Take your time.

걱정하지 마세요. 제가 할게요. → Do not worry. I will do it.

시간 충분하다니까요. → I am telling you, we have enough time.

이 정도면 괜찮을 거예요. → This should be fine.
blocks.speakable: 괜찮아요. 천천히 하세요.  걱정하지 마세요. 제가 할게요.  시간 충분하다니까요.  이 정도면 괜찮을 거예요.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker responds to another person's concern by presenting the situation as manageable, safe, or less serious than feared.
